normalizedSpaces.label: Formal semantics
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ACM curricular and SIGPLAN research structures treat formal semantics as a stable research/knowledge unit with operational, denotational, axiomatic and type-based approaches. Its use extends beyond defining programming-language behavior to formal system modeling, so it is retained as a non-exclusive semantic-modeling axis/subspace rather than equated with all FPL.

normalizedSpaces.label: Formal methods
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ACM sources characterize Formal Methods as a broad family of techniques/tools for specification, development, analysis and verification across software and hardware, including theorem proving, model checking, formal modeling, program logics, type systems and semantics. It is a cross-cutting method/domain, not a single-parent Foundation root.

repair.oldPressure: SCD had strong owner-native semantic/formalization research but the external model only exposed broad Foundations of Programming Languages, making any identity-level mapping either too coarse or falsely owner-like.
repair.repair: Normalize Formal Semantics and Formal Methods as external, non-root, cross-cutting identities.
